title: Where ZIA, ZPA and Client Connector logs can be read, and for how long
aliases: how long are zscaler logs kept
do i need a siem for older logs

prose.text: Each product keeps and exports its logs differently, which decides where a correlation query can run and how far back it can reach.

Web and firewall logs are held in the Nanolog, and each NSS receives copies: [[zia.logs.nss-feed-format:one-store]]. A Cloud NSS instance takes one feed per log type: [[zia.logs.nss-feed-format:cloud-feed-limit]]. The web, firewall and DNS feeds each have their own field set: [[zia/web-log]], [[zia/firewall-log]], [[zia/dns-log]]. VM-based and Cloud NSS deployment is described in [[shared.nss.delivery-modes]], and the feed format specifiers in [[shared.nss.feeds:format-specifiers]].

LSS streams through a Public Service Edge to an App Connector that forwards to the log receiver, and it is separate from NSS: [[zpa.log-receivers.architecture:two-components]], [[zpa.log-receivers.architecture:not-nss]]. A receiver can carry nineteen log types: [[zpa.log-receivers.log-types:help-log-types]]. User Activity, User Status and App Connector logs are retained for at least 14 days and audit logs for at least 6 months: [[zpa.log-receivers.delivery:cloud-retention]]. Data generated during a connection loss is not delivered except as the help describes: [[zpa.app-connectors.health:lss-retransmit-limits]]. Mutual TLS between connector and receiver is optional and has certificate requirements: [[zpa.log-receivers.tls]].

prose.heading: Client Connector: logs on the device

prose.text: Client Connector's log is collected from the device, by user export or an admin fetch: [[zcc.logging.user-access:visible-capabilities]], [[zcc.logging.collection:fetch-prereq]]. Whether it records individual transactions is open: [[zcc.logs.client-log:transaction-records]]. Whether any Client Connector log reaches a SIEM directly is open {{gap:zcc-siem-stream}}; the ZIA view of its traffic is in [[shared.log-correlation.zcc-in-zia]].
Cloud Connector's log paths are described in [[cloud-connector.logs]].

checks.do: Before querying, check that the window is inside what the source still holds: 180 days in the Nanolog for ZIA Insights logs, at least 14 days for ZPA User Activity, User Status and App Connector logs in the console; beyond that only a SIEM copy has it.
For very recent events, allow for ZIA's consolidation latency before concluding a record is missing.

zia-retention.statement: The ZIA Insights Logs article says logs are stored for 180 days in the Zscaler Nanolog servers, and that NSS, a virtual machine, can stream web traffic logs in real time from the Nanolog to a SIEM, enabling real-time alerting, correlation with the logs of firewalls and other devices, and long-term local log archival.

quotes: Logs are stored for 180 days in the Zscaler Nanolog servers.

Zscaler also offers the Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS), a virtual machine (VM) that can stream web traffic logs in real time from the Zscaler Nanolog to your security information and event management (SIEM) system
enabling real-time alerting, correlation with the logs of your firewall and other devices, and long-term local log archival

zia-consolidation-latency.statement: The ZIA Insights Logs article says the Zscaler service performs global time-ordered log consolidation, with a potential latency of several seconds to a few minutes.

quotes: The Zscaler service performs global time-ordered log consolidation, with potential latency ranging from several seconds to a few minutes

zcc-siem-stream.title: Whether any Client Connector log reaches a SIEM directly
zcc-siem-stream.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "ZCC does not produce a SIEM-streamable log feed equivalent to NSS or LSS"; its logs cover tunnel, authentication, posture and forwarding events, and "the SIEM-queryable view of what a ZCC device was doing lives entirely in ZIA NSS." The registered sources describe device-side collection and Flow Logging reports to ZIA, but no page states that Client Connector has no SIEM export.
zcc-siem-stream.blocks: Answering whether Client Connector events can be searched in a SIEM
